meta.title: The Waif
sources: the-waif-demonstration.json and the-waif-preston.json: repeated splitting events and terminal fatal outcomes

worlds.label: The opening world
worlds.description: Opening timeline: the Waif dies when she falls onto the Forester; Jack dies and Marie and Ben survive. Ben leaves at the pre-arrival trigger pull.

worlds.label: The world with her - already running
worlds.description: The Waif’s surviving branch of the fall. It already exists when Ben crosses before scene 78. The exact Ben/Jack accident outcomes in this branch are not supplied.

worlds.label: The world where he died - already running
worlds.description: The accident outcome where Jack lives and Ben dies. The followed Ben enters this established history at his pull in scene 114.

worlds.label: The family world - already running
worlds.description: The reunion world reached at scenes 185–188, with an intact Forester and its own history. The house attack, cabin siege, family deaths, chamber removal and final shot follow here. This is not the independent red-light world.

worlds.label: He dies at the last shot
worlds.description: The fatal outcome of the side-of-head shot at scene 184. Separate from the final mouth shot at 266. Subsequent history is not followed.

worlds.label: The falling-car accident before its outcomes
worlds.description: Author-confirmed common splitting event behind the opening outcome, Jack’s surviving outcome and the Waif’s surviving branch.

worlds.label: Independent parallel closing universe
worlds.description: Runs parallel to the first scenes. The final red-light family has no causal connection to the main narrative. It is not the destination of Ben’s final shot.

agents.label: Ben (opening world)
agents.notes: Ben carries memories between changes and later struggles with conflicting memories. The closing parallel Ben is not a declared continuation of this traveller.

agents.label: The Waif
agents.notes: The living Waif in the alternate world Ben enters. The Waif in the opening world dies. She remembers Ben and their earlier lives; her complete personal itinerary is not specified.

agents.label: The woman who falls (opening world)
agents.notes: Author-confirmed death in the opening timeline. A living Waif already exists in the alternate world Ben enters.

agents.label: Marie
agents.notes: Ben’s wife or estranged partner. She and Jack die outside the cabin in the reunion-world siege. Their closing parallel versions are independent.

agents.label: Jack
agents.notes: Son of Ben and Marie. Dies in the opening crash; alive in the world where Ben died; later dies in the reunion-world siege. His closing parallel version is independent.

agents.label: The Others
agents.notes: Pale-fire figures that have to be looked at to exist. They take the woman apart at the end of a pass and light her up again.

agents.label: Q. R. Preston
agents.notes: Author and armorer. Repeated self-directed attempts branch the universes; Ben takes the revolver and kills him in the followed outcome. See the separate Preston perspective.

agents.label: Jamie
agents.notes: Shopkeeper: the permit and resale conversation concerns a gun, not the cabin.

agents.label: Ben who died before the traveller arrived
agents.notes: Historical death in the earlier branch, distinct from the arriving traveller.

agents.label: Ben (independent closing universe)
agents.notes: No personal-continuity or causal connection to the main narrative is asserted.

events.label: A father watches for danger
events.description: Ben checks the house and sits with Jack, who thinks his reflection moved on its own. The next day the family drives into the city. Marie, in the passenger seat, is working from her equations; Jack rides in the rear.

events.label: The living Waif arrives at the cabin
events.description: Ben is now in the pre-existing world where the Waif is alive. A soaked stranger arrives at his door and persuades him to admit her. Inside, she cuts her foot on the glass he broke earlier. She hopes he will remember her; he does not recognise her.

events.label: She describes surviving branches
events.description: The Waif uses Jack’s blue ball in her explanation. Ben had found it in the cabin at scene 59; cross-world provenance is not established.

events.label: Her account leaves things out
events.description: The Waif recounts abandonment by a man, repeated apparent survivals and confinement. An unseen-faced psychiatrist gives her the book in a padded room. She says Preston killed himself. Later scenes revise the office incident and contradict her account of Preston’s death; this is not an unqualified history.

events.label: His next pull takes him to the world where he died
events.description: With the Waif beside him, Ben pulls the trigger. His experienced outcome is a click, and he enters the world in which Jack is alive and Ben has already died. An earlier split produced that history. The arrival does not create it.

events.label: The followed Ben enters that existing history
events.description: The Ben we follow arrives in the already-branched world where Jack is alive and a Ben died earlier. The traveller and the historical death must not be collapsed into one event.

events.label: The family dies in the pickup
events.description: During the cabin siege, the Waif admits an Other through the back door. Marie takes Jack outside while Ben is pinned. They reach the F-250 pickup, which will not start. The Woman in White crushes its roof. Ben reaches Marie and Jack too late. This follows the reunion and escape in the same presented sequence.

payload.note: Author continuity clarification, 2026-09-13; March numbered screenplay; Scenes 240–253

events.label: She disables the special chamber
events.description: The Others approach Ben but do not take him. He briefly closes his eyes, then opens them and looks at the figures. Inside, the Waif removes the radioactive chamber and says the gun will now fire every time. She asks him to kill her, promising the erasure of his pain and memories.

payload.note: Author continuity clarification, 2026-09-13; March numbered screenplay; Scenes 255–256

events.label: The jumper was the Waif
events.description: The office incident is revisited: she fired through the window and jumped. Flashbacks connect her fall to the Forester, and Ben sees the same red-striped shoes. She says she was the jumper. Her continuity across these lives is part of the revelation; the screenplay does not supply a complete counterpart map.

events.label: The Waif asks him to kill her
events.description: She asks Ben to shoot her and promises that the pain and memories of his family will vanish. He ultimately turns the gun on himself at 266.

events.label: Ben tries again after the failed reunion
events.description: After the failed reunion, Ben holds the gun to the side of his head and pulls the trigger. The fatal outcome is followed at the end of 184 and the surviving perspective resumes in 185. This is not the final shot at 266.

payload.note: Author continuity clarification, 2026-09-13; March numbered screenplay; Scene 184, before the discharge

events.label: The Others take her
events.description: The Others corner the Waif and tear her apart, merging into her flesh. She later emerges with their strange gait, pale skin and dead eyes. She extinguishes the fire with a snap of her fingers. This is a transformation, not a demonstrated restoration to her earlier state.

payload.note: Author continuity clarification, 2026-09-13; March numbered screenplay; Scenes 267–270

events.label: The film resumes with a surviving Ben
events.description: Ben wakes on the floor, alone, with a scorch mark described as a misfire. Five rounds remain. The cabin is intact and lived in, its books and possessions back in place. Outside sits the undamaged Forester. His experience now continues in a reality with a different history.

This universe has no causal connection to the main narrative. Its family is not the result of Ben’s final shot.

events.description: The author identifies the accident as the fork: Ben lives and Jack dies in the opening outcome; Jack lives and Ben dies in the other. The Waif also has a fatal outcome and a surviving branch. Her surviving world exists before Ben’s first crossing.

events.label: This world already lost Ben
events.description: The accident’s other family outcome kills Ben and leaves Jack alive. This is the historical death in the world the followed Ben later enters at 114. The arrival does not cause or replace that earlier death.

events.label: Ben’s final shot
events.description: After the radioactive chamber has been removed, Ben aims at the Waif. A fallen photograph recalls his family. He then puts the gun in his own mouth and fires. His body falls and the Others turn on her. The independent red-light universe is not a surviving destination of this act.

events.label: The robbery and planted gun are revealed
events.description: At the cabin, the Waif reveals a shared criminal past. Flashbacks show them robbing Preston, Ben taking the revolver and shooting him, and Ben hiding the box beside the cabin wiring. Ben partly recognises these memories while resisting them. The Waif says their many lives have become tangled; the exact placement of that earlier life remains unspecified.

ruleEffects.effect: Removing the radioactive chamber makes every later pull fire, so each pull produces its own split outcomes.

interventions.notes: The Waif removes the radioactive chamber at 256 and says the gun will now fire every time.

ruleEffects.effect: Ben turns the final pull on himself; any surviving continuation is left unspecified and is not the independent closing universe.

interventions.notes: The Waif asks him to shoot her, but he turns the gun on himself at 266. The closing universe is causally independent.

outcome.summary: Ben crosses before 78 into a pre-existing world with a living Waif, and at 114 into an earlier branch where Jack lives and Ben died. His reunion at 185 leads into the siege and final shot at 266. The closing red-light family belongs to an independent parallel universe running alongside the opening; no main-narrative event causes it.

semanticReview.note: Authorial clarification 2026-09-13 governs the crossings before 78 and at 114, the Waif’s first-world death, and the causally independent closing world. DRAFT indicates pending editorial review, not uncertainty about that supplied canon.

184 and 266 are distinct acts in the governing screenplay. Earlier composite events and their review notes have been replaced. Narrative source references point to the March draft and the new author statement.

This legacy format remains a secondary projection. The Waif’s complete earlier-lives map and exact personal crossings are not specified. Read the authored Ben, Waif and Preston documents for scoped explanations.

Author identifies the earlier split as the opening accident: Ben lives / Jack dies and Jack lives / Ben dies. The Waif also has a surviving branch. DRAFT retains pending reader review, not unidentified ancestry.
